verdict.rationale: Elasticsearch documents a code-first path: a one-line local install, official client libraries, and a flow where you 'create an index mapping to start ingesting, embedding, and querying data.' It also has an official MCP server repo and official skills that teach coding agents to work with the stack. A community note says newly indexed documents may not be searchable until refresh, but that is configurable. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of the REST/CLI calls for index creation, ingestion and querying; details of which operations the MCP server exposes (e.g. writes vs read-only); hands-on corroboration of an agent completing the flow, especially since the llms.txt and site-root OpenAPI probes returned 404.
